title: What is your name?
goal: Say 'my name is ...', ask 'what is your name?' to a man and to a woman, answer with ahlan, and bounce the question back with 'and you?'.

items.note: The simplest introduction: أنا (I) + your name. Arabic has no word for 'am'.

items.mnemonic: ISM: every NAME ends up an '-ISM' (Tom-ism, Julie-ism).

items.note: Hook an 'i' sound on the end of a word and it belongs to me: ism (name) → ismi (my name).
items.mnemonic: is-MI: 'this name IS ME' = MY name.

items.note: أهلاً literally means 'welcome'; it is what you say when you meet someone, so it works as 'nice to meet you'.
items.mnemonic: AH-lan: 'AH, LAND here, welcome!' nice to meet you.

items.note: Swap the -i (my) for -uka (your, to a man): ismi → ismuka.

items.en: what is your name? (to a man)
items.note: Word for word: what your-name? No 'is'.

items.en: what is your name? (to a man)

items.note: أهلاً + the person's name is the natural reply once someone tells you their name.

items.en: name / my name / your name (to a man)
items.note: Quick recap of the three forms before the female form.
To a woman the ending is -ki instead of -ka: ismuka (to a man) → ismuki (to a woman).

items.en: what is your name? (to a woman)
you (to a man) / you (to a woman)
items.note: Same word, different ending: anta to a man, anti to a woman. It matches the -ka / -ki of ismuka / ismuki.
و (wa, 'and') sticks to the front of أنتَ, said with question intonation.

items.en: my name is Julie, and you?
you (to a woman) / you (to a man)
items.note: She shows each form alone, then side by side.

items.en: and you, what's your name? (to a woman)
items.note: Her card writes 'ma' for ما here; it is the same word as maa.

items.en: and you, what's your name? (to a man)
you (to a man) / you (to a woman)
items.note: Quiz: which one do you say to a woman? anti.

items.en: my name / your name (to a man)
items.note: Quiz: which one is 'my name'? ismi.

items.en: what is your name? (to a man)
items.note: Quiz: 'ma ismuka?' or 'ma ismuko?' The correct one is ismuka, with the -a ending for a man.

dialogue.en: Hello. I am Julie. What is your name?
My name is Ahmad. Nice to meet you, Julie.

dialogue.ar: أهلاً أحمد. أنا أريدُ أن أتعلّم العربية.
dialogue.tr: ahlan Ahmad. ana oreedo an ataa'llam al a'rabiya.
dialogue.en: Nice to meet you, Ahmad. I want to learn Arabic.

dialogue.ar: أنا أيضاً أتعلّم الإنجليزية. هل أنتِ من هنا؟
dialogue.tr: ana aydan ataa'llam al injleeziya. hal anti min huna?
dialogue.en: I am also learning English. Are you from here?

dialogue.ar: لا، أنا لستُ من هنا. أنا أفهمُ العربية قليلاً.
dialogue.tr: la, ana lastu min huna. ana afhamu al a'rabiya qaleelan.
dialogue.en: No, I am not from here. I understand Arabic a little.
